title: Soviet prisoners of war in German captivity
summary: Soviet prisoners held by Germany from 1941 to 1945 died in very large numbers. The USHMM says more than three million died in custody, mostly of malnutrition and exposure, with about 2,000,000 of 3,300,000 dead by February 1942. Encyclopedia.com reports 5.7 million captured and a range of at least 2.53 million to 3.3 million deaths.

importance.justification: One of the largest groups of victims of Nazi policy; USHMM ranks Soviet POWs second only to the Jews.

audience_note: Describes mass starvation, disease and killing of prisoners, including gassing. Death figures are attributed: USHMM, more than three million died in German custody and about 2,000,000 of 3,300,000 by February 1942; encyclopedia.com, at least 2.53 million up to 3.3 million (Streit, 1997) of 5.7 million captured. Estimates differ by source.
